high_level_description: Wordless museum-catalog illustration in the historical visual language of Nevers faience: three equal tin-glazed plates independently emphasize different objects from one shared collection, each bearing a separate maker seal, while identical scale and spacing prevent any plate from becoming a universal ranking; cobalt, green, yellow, and manganese on white.

compositional_deconstruction.background: A whitewashed pottery-gallery wall contains three equal shallow alcoves in one horizontal row above a pale limestone floor. Each alcove has identical dimensions, height, illumination, and plain molding. The middle position has no brighter light, larger frame, raised base, canopy, crown, trophy, or special ornament. Empty space surrounds all three equally. No inscription, letter, numeral, caption, arrow, pointer, podium, ranking mark, or central emblem appears anywhere.

elements.desc: Left Nevers-faience display plate, exactly equal in scale to the other two, with white tin glaze and a narrow cobalt rim. Six pictorial medallions occupy the same two-by-three positions used on every plate; bridge, seedling, and mallet are fully colored while lantern, wheel, and blank folio remain pale outlines. A green three-loop maker seal hangs below.

Middle Nevers-faience display plate, exactly equal in scale to the other two, with white tin glaze and the same narrow cobalt rim. Six matching medallions retain the shared two-by-three order; lantern, wheel, and blank folio are fully colored while bridge, seedling, and mallet remain pale outlines. A violet concentric-ring maker seal hangs below, without extra ornament.

Right Nevers-faience display plate, exactly equal in scale to the other two, with white tin glaze and the same narrow cobalt rim. Six matching medallions retain the shared two-by-three order; bridge, wheel, and blank folio are fully colored while lantern, seedling, and mallet remain pale outlines. An ochre crosshatched maker seal hangs below, matching the others in size.

Long low glass vitrine with a dark-blue ceramic base, treated as one enclosure with its contents. Inside, six white-glazed models stand at equal height: arched bridge, hooded lantern, potted seedling, water wheel, carpenter's mallet, and closed blank folio. Their shapes recur on every plate; the case has no label, preferred object, or central pedestal.
